title: Energy stores and systems

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Energy store
items.clue: A way in which a system holds energy.

items.label: Kinetic store
items.clue: The store filled when an object moves.

items.label: Gravitational potential store
items.clue: The store filled when an object is raised.

items.label: Energy transfer
items.clue: The moving of energy from one store to another.

questions.stem: In physics, what is meant by a system?

options.text: An object, or a group of objects, being studied.
A machine that has been built to move energy.
A group of two or more objects, never one.
A place where energy is kept until used.

questions.explanation: This is the specification's definition: a system is an object or group of objects.

questions.stem: What always happens when a system changes?

options.text: Some of the energy in the system is used up.
The way energy is stored in the system changes.
The amount of energy in the system rises.
Extra energy is created inside the system itself.

questions.explanation: This is exactly what the specification says happens when a system changes.

questions.stem: Which of these is a way of storing energy rather than a way of transferring it?

options.text: The heating of a large beaker of cold water.
The work done by a steady pushing force.
The elastic store of a squashed spring.
An electric current in a copper wire.

questions.explanation: A stretched or squashed spring holds energy, so this is a store.

questions.stem: The specification asks for all the changes in the way energy is stored when a system changes. What must such a description name?

options.text: Only the store that empties during the change.
Only the useful store that fills in the change.
The size of the force that is acting on the system.
Each store that empties and each that fills.

questions.explanation: 'All the changes' means both ends of every transfer are named.

questions.stem: A ball is thrown straight upwards. As it rises, what happens to the way energy is stored?

options.text: The gravitational store empties, the kinetic store fills.
The kinetic store empties and the gravitational store fills.
The kinetic store keeps filling while the ball rises.
Both the kinetic and the gravitational stores fill.

questions.explanation: The ball slows as it gains height, so the kinetic store empties into the gravitational store.

questions.stem: Air resistance is ignored. At the highest point of a ball's flight, what has happened to the energy that was in its kinetic store?

options.text: It was destroyed at the moment the ball stopped.
It has been transferred to the elastic store of the air.
Some remains, because the ball is still moving up.
It has all been transferred to the gravitational store.

questions.explanation: With no air resistance the whole of the kinetic store fills the gravitational store.

questions.stem: A trolley moving along a bench hits a wall and stops. What happens to the energy in its kinetic store?

options.text: It is transferred to thermal stores and by sound.
It is destroyed by the impact of the trolley on the wall.
It is used up in bringing the trolley to a stop.
It stays in the kinetic store of the stopped trolley.

questions.explanation: The trolley, the wall and the surrounding air warm slightly and a sound wave carries some energy away.

questions.stem: A constant horizontal force pushes a box along a smooth, level floor. Which store fills as the box speeds up?

options.text: The gravitational store of the moving box.
The chemical store of the pushing force.
The kinetic store of the moving box.
The elastic store of the smooth floor.

questions.explanation: Work done by the force transfers energy to the kinetic store as the box speeds up.

questions.stem: A car slows down when the driver brakes. Which statement describes the changes in the way energy is stored?

options.text: The kinetic store empties into the chemical store of the brakes.
Energy is lost from the car, so the total energy falls.
The kinetic store empties and the thermal stores of the brakes fill.
The kinetic store of the car fills as it keeps moving.

questions.explanation: Friction at the brakes does work, filling thermal stores of the brakes, tyres, road and air.

questions.stem: A cyclist stops pedalling on level ground and slowly freewheels to a stop. Which store empties?

options.text: The kinetic store of the cyclist and the bicycle.
The chemical store held in the cyclist's leg muscles.
The gravitational store of the moving bicycle.
No store keeps it, the energy is lost to the surroundings.

questions.explanation: Friction and air resistance do work, emptying the kinetic store into thermal stores.

questions.stem: Water is brought to the boil in an electric kettle. Which statement describes the main change in the way energy is stored?

options.text: The chemical store of the kettle itself empties into the water.
The water gains a store of electrical energy as it is heated.
The kinetic store of the water fills as the water boils.
The current does work and the water's thermal store fills.

questions.explanation: A current in the element does work; the thermal stores of the element and then the water fill.

questions.stem: As well as the water, which other thermal stores fill while a kettle boils?

options.text: Only the water's store; nothing else becomes warm.
Those of the kettle and of the air around it.
None, because the water uses up all the energy.
Those of the mains cable and the power supply.

questions.explanation: The element, the kettle body and the surrounding air all end up warmer.
